full_judgment: 3. The plaint case was that the suit land originally belonged to Zohuruddin, Kerali Sarder, Goni and Yousuf Ali and their names were recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 263. There was an amicable partition amongst the C.S. recorded tenants, Kerali Sarder got 0.56 acre land from Plot No. 907 and .23 acre land from Plot No. 908, Kerali Sarder was satisfied with the above .79 acre land though he was entitled to get more land in his share. Kerali Sarder died leaving behind four sons named Akkel Ali, Nowab Ali, Mnsur Ali and Abdus Samad and two daughters named Amina Begum and Moroni Begum. Kerali Sarder during his life time by the sale deed dated 03.06.1921 transferred .17 acre land from Plot No. 908 and .14 acre land from Plot No. 907 in favour of his son, Akkel Ali vide deed No. 3799. Then on 03.06.1925, Kerali Sarder again by sale deed No. 3798 transferred 23 acre land from Plot No. 908 and .17 acre land from Plot No. 907, i.e. in total .40 acre land to his son, Nowab Ali. The plaintiff as the heir of Monsur Ali, son of Kerali Sarder, inherited 2-1/3 acre land and subsequently, he, on 02.02.1989, purchased 19½ acre land from Rahima and others and on 19.02.1990, also purchased 3½ acre land from the heirs of Moroni Begum and thus the plaintiff got in total 24½ acre land by purchase. The plaintiff had been possessing the suit land peacefully by paying rent etc, but the defendants were trying to evict the plaintiff from the suit land and hence the suit.
